clues: This place sits on flat farm land in the center of its state, by a river. Roads from all sides cross here, so folks call it a crossroads.
Spring days here can trick you badly. A warm day in March or April can end with snow falling just a day or two later.
This place was planned from scratch in 1821 to be the new seat of government. Its streets were laid out in a neat grid on one square mile.
Each year this place hosts a famed car race known all around the world. It is the largest one-day sports event in the whole world.
This place is the seat of government for Indiana. Its governor and its state lawmakers both work here.
